claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
The proposed intervention is partial substitution of Hf with Nb.
Partial substitution of Hf with Nb reduces the alloy's average atomic mass.
Partial substitution of Hf with Nb can decrease the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy can maintain or improve strength at room temperature.
The modified alloy can maintain or improve strength at elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
Optimizing alloy composition and microstructure may maintain or improve mechanical properties after Nb substitution.
The proposed temperature range is room temperature through 1000 °C.
The hypothesis is limited to loading conditions below those causing significant deformation or failure in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes loading that causes significant deformation or failure, while measuring strength conventionally requires loading into substantial plastic deformation or failure; the proposed test therefore may fall outside the stated boundary.

The hypothesis and uncertainty allow for an unknown optimal Nb substitution ratio, but the rejection rule says that a strength decrease in any tested partially substituted sample falsifies the hypothesis. A poor nonoptimal composition would not contradict the existence of another successful substitution ratio.
